p1: [low, ominous] My grandfather watched the house in the nineteen twenties. [low] My father watched in the nineteen sixties. [whispers] It is now my time.
[low] That letter was waiting for a family... who had just bought a house in Westfield, New Jersey.
[low] June, twenty fourteen. They paid about one point three million dollars. [low, tense] They hadn't even moved in yet.
[low] It was typed. [low, ominous] And it was signed... [whispers] The Watcher.
[low, tense] More letters came. The writer called the house... [whispers] my job, my life, my obsession.
[whispers] Who am I? [low, ominous] I am the Watcher.
[low, cold] The family never moved in. [low] Not one night.
[low] Police investigated. So did private investigators... and former FBI agents.
[low, ominous] No one... was ever charged.
[low] In twenty nineteen, they sold the house for nine hundred fifty-nine thousand dollars. [low, cold] A huge loss.
[low] To this day, no one knows who The Watcher is... [whispers] or if they're still watching.
